decisions.if_role_rebinds: a deployable role editor (detector masks, inpainting) and the role arm on every task with a role code (13 of the 71 failing tasks) on practice states follow; the attention arms of b_bind_q2 are read by their own rule
decisions.role_rebinds: BA >= 0.5 on at least 2 of the 4 tasks
decisions.role_steerable: roleplacebo binds its placebo object in >= 0.5 of its episodes pooled

metrics.episodes: 10 per arm and task, practice init states 0-9, client --bind track (episodes run to success or the step limit)
metrics.measures: BA = share of episodes whose first movable object displaced > 3 cm while the commanded gripper is closed is the task's moved instance; success (the task's own BDDL check); for roleplacebo, the share binding the placebo object

new_arms.role: the task prototype the policy performs in the same scene with the same relation and target instance (lifelong_ood/policy/roles.py role_code: 48 -> 46, 49 -> 46, 52 -> 50, 53 -> 50), under ITS instruction, with the new task's object and the base's object exchanging appearance in the simulator's renderer (client --swap a:b --swap-mode render; ORACLE: perfect rendering; physics untouched); the policy generates every action
new_arms.roleplacebo: steerability: the same, with the base's object exchanging appearance with a movable object the task does not name (roles.placebo_code: 48 tomato sauce, 49 ketchup, 52 tomato sauce, 53 tomato sauce)

metrics.why: the offline probes (b1, b2) found that the action expert already attends the named object under the task's own instruction on most living-room frames while the policy still moves the routine's object; biasing attention turns the first chunk toward the biased object (contrast cosine) without changing which object it heads for. If the routine is driven by what the objects LOOK like, rebinding the role in the observation should work where attention does not.
metrics.written_before: any episode of the role or roleplacebo arms
